title: Sind-Habbari Dynasty
capsule: The Habbari emirate was an Arab Muslim dynasty descended from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Habbari that governed Sindh from its capital at Mansurah, ruling as a semi-autonomous emirate that nominally acknowledged Abbasid suzerainty from the mid-9th century onward. Across the period covered here the Habbaris controlled the lower Indus basin and its agrarian and mercantile economy, with trade links to the Persian Gulf and Iraq described in the Arabic geographers al-Mas'udi and Ibn Hawqal. Habbari rule did not endure to the end of this window: the Ghaznavid sultan Mahmud campaigned against Mansurah around 1025-1026, destroying the city and annexing Sindh, so that effective Habbari authority was extinguished in the first quarter of the eleventh century rather than persisting into the twelfth.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Arabic geographical accounts place the Habbari in the lower Indus region with reasonable confidence; exact northern and eastern boundaries are not precisely attested in the sources.
